findings.title: Deleting a cooked personal recipe makes the kitchen's own backup unrestorable
findings.input: Create/cook a personal recipe R002, delete it, export, then restore the exported file.
findings.actual: parseBackup returns ok:false because the preserved cook event references a recipe removed from the active book. A recipeName snapshot does not satisfy the validator.
findings.fix: Keep a historical recipe tombstone/version, or explicitly validate historical references with their snapshots while resolving active plan references on deletion.

findings.title: Recovered pending settings are saved but never applied to the booted UI
findings.input: Persist a pending settings operation with defaultServings:7 while the saved database has 4; reopen the app.
findings.actual: IndexedDB becomes 7, but Settings shows 4. A subsequent whole-settings write built from the stale UI can overwrite recovered values.
findings.fix: Apply settings operations in the pending-state reducer before creating KitchenStore; cover all KitchenWrite variants and preserve operation order.

findings.title: Restore clears the cart only on screen; old manual items return after reload
findings.input: Save a manual six-egg shopping line, restore a backup, open Shop (line gone), reload, open Shop again.
findings.actual: The six-egg line reappears. The shopping store is absent from backup data and replacement transactions; App only calls setShopList([]).
findings.fix: Include the manual shopping list in backup/pre-restore-copy/replacement state. If restore intentionally clears it, at minimum clear it durably in the replacement transaction.

findings.title: Editing a recipe silently turns optional ingredients into required ingredients
findings.input: Open a recipe containing an optional ingredient, change only its name, and save.
findings.actual: The saved ingredient no longer has optional:true. Availability and the shopping basket now treat it as required.
findings.fix: Carry the optional flag through the editor form and reconstruction, including rows that were not otherwise changed.

findings.title: The open app does not refresh its household day at midnight
findings.input: Leave Today open at Karachi 2026-10-05 23:59; advance to 2026-10-06 00:01 without another interaction.
findings.actual: The header stays Monday · 5 October. Day/time-derived plan and recommendation state has no clock-triggered refresh.
findings.fix: Use a household clock state that updates at relevant boundaries and on visibility/focus resume, with deterministic midnight tests.

findings.title: The Gemini timeout stops when headers arrive, leaving a stalled response body unbounded
findings.input: Fetch returns HTTP 200 headers immediately, but its JSON body never completes.
findings.actual: The abort timer is cleared before res.json(). A configured 10 ms timeout has not aborted the request after 50 ms.
findings.fix: Keep the timeout and abort handling alive through body consumption/parsing; return a timeout GeminiError for a body abort.

findings.title: Automatic retries bypass the advertised physical-request rate limit
findings.input: maxPerMinute:1, retries:1; first response is HTTP 503, second is HTTP 200.
findings.actual: Two HTTP requests are made inside the one-request window. At the default configuration, 12 calls can issue up to 24 HTTP requests.
findings.fix: Reserve/check a rate-limit slot for every physical attempt, including retries, using the current time.

findings.title: Malformed response envelopes bypass the structured error boundary
findings.input: Return valid JSON null, content.parts:'invalid', or groundingChunks:{}.
findings.actual: The client throws raw TypeError values instead of GeminiError('bad-response'). The UI's generic catch prevents a demonstrated whole-app crash; structured classification/retry handling is lost.
findings.fix: Runtime-validate the response object and each accessed array/entry before reading fields; reject malformed envelopes with a controlled error.

findings.title: Restore accepts a repayment amount that contradicts the all/half rule
findings.input: Import an order of Rs 2401 with repay:{option:'half',amount:1}.
findings.actual: Validation accepts it; owedTotal trusts the stored amount, so a restored half repayment is Rs 1 rather than Rs 1201.
findings.fix: Validate repayment amount against the order cost and option using the same whole-rupee rule; reject contradictory backup values.

findings.title: Equal timestamp stock checks are ordered by random ID rather than recorded sequence
findings.input: At the same millisecond, record set-stock 5 with id z-first, then set-stock 2 with id a-second.
findings.actual: balances([first,second]) returns 5. ID ordering reverses which stock check wins. Production frequency is not established; the existing browser helpers avoid equal timestamps.
findings.fix: Persist an explicit recording sequence (including legacy/import migration) so equal-time stock anchors have an authoritative order.

findings.title: The request byte limit counts UTF-16 characters
findings.input: Set maxRequestBytes:500 and send 'نور'.repeat(100). The text alone is 600 UTF-8 bytes; the serialized request is 391 characters and 691 bytes.
findings.actual: The request is sent despite exceeding the byte cap. The corrected regression independently checks the UTF-8 payload size.
findings.fix: Measure the serialized body with TextEncoder().encode(body).byteLength before sending.

findings.title: A finite quantity can overflow during conversion and poison saved stock
findings.input: toBase(1e308,'kg',rice), or Bought more with the equivalent plain decimal input.
findings.actual: Conversion and the pantry event builder both return ok:true, with an Infinity movement. JSON serialization turns Infinity into null, which is not a valid saved movement delta.
findings.fix: Reject non-finite converted/rounded results and impose a reasonable pantry input bound before event creation.
